feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start = "On April 2, 2000, the RHIC team began injecting gold ions into the blue ring" (BNL RHIC 25 timeline, src:heavy-ions-rhic25-timeline), the first dated injection; RHIC was dedicated on 4 October 1999 after commissioning, whose beam dates are not given. End = RHIC's final run, 6 February 2026; the AGS is planned to feed the Electron-Ion Collider (no Atlas record yet). Transfer line: the AGS-to-RHIC (AtR) line, per the RHIC Accelerators page.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: the AGS receives protons and other ions from the AGS Booster and delivers them to the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider after acceleration.

feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: Lovelace et al., IPAC2022 WEPOTK014, abstract; Introduction
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Planned, not yet in operation. The EIC's Hadron Storage Ring is one of the RHIC rings; its hadrons come through the existing injector chain: "The beam is transported through two accelerators, the AGS-booster and the AGS, to the HSR injection energy and extracted through a transfer line to the HSR." (same paper; polarised protons start from the 200 MeV linac). BNL: "the other RHIC ring, refurbished for its new mission, will receive ions accelerated by C-AD’s existing injector complex" (src:heavy-ions-rhic-final-collisions-2026). The date window is from the ePIC paper: "The EIC project detector is expected to start operate in 2032" (arXiv:2305.15593). The AGS to RHIC link ends on 2026-02-06 with RHIC's final run.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: To accomplish the acceleration process, the hadrons are pre-accelerated in the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron (AGS), extracted, and transferred to HSR for injection.

start.display: planned; the EIC's start of operations is not dated in the sources read (2032 is the 2023 expectation for the ePIC detector, which may have moved)

intervals.label: RHIC injector (24 GeV protons)
intervals.locator: Aidala et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 85, 655 (arXiv:1209.2803), §II.A
intervals.note: Start/end as on the AGS to RHIC relationship. Gold ions left the AGS at 8.86 GeV per nucleon: "The nominal momentum and kinetic energy at extraction are 9.75 GeV/c and 8.86 GeV per nucleon (γ = 10.520)." (Ahrens et al., PAC 2001). The 33 GeV top-level beam_energy is the AGS design energy for protons.

name: Alternating Gradient Synchrotron
notes: RHIC, the main current user of this accelerator's beam, completed its final run on 2026-02-06 and is being converted into the Electron-Ion Collider (src:bnl-newsroom-eic-transformation-2026). No source consulted states whether or how AGS operations have changed since; the status 'active' is carried forward from the present-tense official page of 2026-09-17 and should be re-checked once BNL publishes the AGS's post-RHIC operating plan.
No source consulted gives the AGS circumference, so none is recorded under specs.

Injector chain: Linac (200 MeV) to Booster (1.5 GeV protons) to AGS (24 GeV protons, or 8.86 GeV per nucleon for gold) to RHIC. The AGS 'receives protons and other ions from the AGS Booster and delivers them to the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider after acceleration' (src:bnl-rhic-ags-page).

summary.plain: A ring-shaped particle accelerator at Brookhaven National Laboratory, running since 1960. It once held the world speed record for protons and its experiments won three Nobel Prizes; today it accelerates particles before feeding them into other machines, including the RHIC collider.
summary.technical: Brookhaven's Alternating Gradient Synchrotron, commissioned in 1960 using the strong-focusing (alternating-gradient) principle invented there; reached a design energy of 33 GeV for protons. Now serves as part of the injector chain that accelerates protons and heavy ions before delivery to the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider.
